claims.text: Combining ab initio KKR-CPA calculations with experimental transport studies will improve prediction of heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach will avoid conflating lattice and electronic contributions to heat transport.
KKR-CPA combined with experiments can capture the atomic-scale complexity of HfNbTaTiZr and its effects on thermal conductivity.
The proposed model applies to bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystals both with and without defects.
The relevant atomic-scale complexity includes lattice distortions.
The relevant atomic-scale complexity includes electronic structure.
Integrating simulations and experiments permits separate consideration of lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
Separately treating lattice and electronic contributions provides a more accurate understanding of heat-transport mechanisms.
The proposed approach will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% relative to earlier approaches.
The predicted thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr is 12–15 W/(K m) from 300 to 1200 K.
The proposed approach is applicable below 200 K.
The proposed approach is applicable from 300 to 1200 K.
The proposed approach is applicable to some specimens containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Defects may affect the accuracy of the predictions.
Oxygen impurities may affect the accuracy of the predictions.
Predictions should be compared with thermal-conductivity measurements below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted thermal conductivity deviates from experiment by more than 30% in either the low- or high-temperature regime.
